bib.title: Think Bayes, ch. 2: Computational Statistics
bib.venue: book chapter (Think Bayes, 1st ed., Green Tea Press / O'Reilly, 2012; no journal)

question: How can a Bayesian update be coded once so that each new problem only supplies a likelihood?

results.claim: Cookie problem solved with a Pmf: multiply each prior by its likelihood, normalise, Bowl 1 = 0.6.
results.setup: Pmf of two hypotheses, priors 0.5 each, likelihoods 0.75 and 0.5

results.claim: Cookie, Monty Hall and M&M differ only in Likelihood; Update is identical (Suite class, template-method pattern).
The same Suite code gives the M&M posterior 0.7407 for A, i.e. 20/27.
Drawing several cookies with replacement is just repeated Update calls; without replacement the likelihood depends on earlier draws (exercise).
results.quote: the likelihood of each draw depends on the previous draws

limits: Code is the book's own thinkbayes.py in Python 2; no timing or scale results.
practices: Represent a distribution as a map from value to probability and normalise after each update (p.11-13).
Encapsulate the update in an abstract Suite whose subclasses provide only Likelihood (p.16-19).

terms.definition: probability mass function, here a Python dictionary from value to probability
